# Public final generic instance names

An owned Kotlin public abstract class declares a final synthetic inline instance method
with a JVM name Java cannot declare. Its method formal belongs only to that
method; the callback keeps its original contravariant argument and Unit result.
A known superclass may come from source or an immutable SDK declaration JAR.

The Java observer checks direct facade calls and inherited reflective calls,
receiver and callback identity, scalar arguments, callback bridge casts, nulls,
short circuits, partial effects and exact unchecked/checked throwable identity.
Ten independently compiled wrong programs must fail before decompilation. Every
emitted Java unit is compiled; original identities and metadata are compared,
allowing only reported method aliases/helpers, the original synthetic method
flag, Kotlin source filenames and known D8 CLASS annotation loss. The private
application is not part of this fixture.

The owned compiler omits optional inline source debug extensions. The original
method Signature and compiler-generated synthetic flag remain unmodified.
